hints.title: Missing Value Handling
hints.text: Finding the second distinct value requires skipping ties and the maximum value. What query structure guarantees that an empty result set converts cleanly into a single row containing a null value?

hints.title: Distinct Paging and Scalar Subquery
hints.text: Deduplicating entries before ranking ensures identical amounts do not occupy multiple positions. Wrapping the selected value in a scalar subquery converts an empty row count into a null result.

hints.title: Offset Selection with Subquery Fallback
hints.text: Sort unique salary values in descending order using distinct values and select the second entry with limit 1 offset 1. Wrap this statement inside an outer query as a scalar subquery so that if no second distinct salary exists, null is returned.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT (
  SELECT DISTINCT salary
  FROM Employee
  ORDER BY salary DESC
  LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1
) AS SecondHighestSalary;
```

complexity.notes: Scalar subquery wrapping DISTINCT salary ordering with LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Using SELECT DISTINCT salary ... LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1 directly without a wrapper subquery or NULL-coalesce returns zero rows (an empty set) instead of null when the table contains fewer than 2 distinct salaries, failing the LeetCode schema contract.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Wrapping the scalar query in SELECT (...) AS SecondHighestSalary evaluates in O(N log N) time (or O(N) with an index scan on salary DESC) with O(1) memory, returning null automatically upon an empty result set.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling the edge cases where all salaries are identical or only 1 employee exists (must return null); deduplicating with DISTINCT before ordering.
